name: Tenmoku iron glaze
summary: A thick glaze with a high share of iron oxide. In a reduction firing the iron forms streaks, spots and a dark, glassy body.
how: Mix a glaze with 5 to 9 per cent of iron oxide.
Dip the bowl and wipe the glaze from the foot.
Fire in reduction to 1250 to 1320 °C and hold the peak.
Cool slowly, so that iron crystals grow in the glaze.

origin.note: Jian potters of the Song dynasty make dark bowls for whisked tea, with streaks and spots that the kiln forms.

adoptions.via: Jian kilns dip stoneware tea bowls in an iron glaze and fire them in reduction.
